minute_key: kline open time (ms since epoch, UTC); the minute [t, t+60000) owns t and does not own t+60000
boundary_rule: No minute before prospective_from is scientific evidence; minutes before it are engineering data and are excluded from every scientific report, permanently and whatever the contract is later amended to say. While prospective_from is null the boundary has not been fixed and no minute recorded under this contract is scientific evidence. Activation is a reviewed Git commit and never a runtime action: the recorder observes, and a separate pull request writes the boundary. The eligibility evidence is one complete qualifying hour observed by the designated production deployment running under this contract's pre-activation hash. The activation commit sets prospective_from to the earliest UTC midnight that is both after that qualifying hour and strictly after the activation change has merged, so the deployment can be switched to the activated identity before the boundary; the earliest such midnight is the boundary, and any later one would be a boundary chosen rather than derived. Activation changes contract_hash, and the activated hash writes to a fresh storage root: a storage root never mixes contract hashes, the pre-activation engineering root keeps its own hash and is never rewritten or relabelled, and no manifest, normalized day, raw event or heartbeat recorded before activation becomes prospective because the contract was later activated. The activated root may hold engineering observations recorded before the boundary; only observations at or after prospective_from count toward the coverage streak. The boundary is written once and is immutable thereafter. The campaign start instant is named separately by the forward protocol and must be at or after prospective_from plus the review period.

sealed_regions_inherited.p4_hold: the gen1 hold-out region, retired unread by data/research/p4_holdout_ledger.json; no generation reopens it
sealed_regions_inherited.styx: the gen1 sealed test region, from the sealed instant in nn/research_contracts/btc-usdt-1h-gen1.json onward; it is a repository non-read seal with a hindsight-era ceiling, not prospective blind evidence, and it stays sealed

checksum_scheme: SHA-256 over the gzipped raw event file and over the normalized Parquet bytes, recorded in the day manifest and the day metadata. The identity of a normalized day is the value-level digest chimera.recorder-minutes/1, taken over a domain prefix, a canonical header naming the market and its columns, the row count, and then per column a null mask followed by the values as fixed-width little-endian bytes; it is a function of the published numbers and of nothing else, so a re-encoding, a different compression, a different row-group layout or a different pyarrow version cannot move it, and changing one published number does.
coverage_rule: Required streams come in two index kinds, are counted in different units, and the membership of each kind is derived from required_for_coverage rather than restated, so a change to the required set cannot leave a stale partition behind. Minute-indexed: every stream in required_for_coverage other than the settlement-indexed one. Settlement-indexed: um.funding, and it is the only stream of that kind. A stream is in required_for_coverage only when a contemporary first-party archive covering the prospective period publishes a minute denominator for it; a required stream without one would make the gate form a quotient it has no denominator for. For each UTC day D and each minute-indexed required stream s: published_minutes(s, D) is the set of minutes of D present in the Binance daily archive for s, which is futures/um/daily/klines for um.kline_1m, futures/um/daily/markPriceKlines for um.markPrice and spot/daily/klines for spot.kline_1m; captured_minutes(s, D) is the set of minutes of D present in the recorder's normalized file for s whose values agree with the archive within tolerance; published_coverage(s, D) = |captured intersect published| / |published|; wallclock_coverage(s, D) = |captured| / 1440. um.markPrice is one required stream with one verdict from one source family: its archive criterion is the mark-price agreement criterion supported by futures/um/daily/markPriceKlines and nothing else. The index values the live mark-price observations hold alongside the mark are recorded, and they may be reconciled against futures/um/daily/indexPriceKlines and reported as a diagnostic, but index agreement is not a second pass condition for um.markPrice coverage and no threshold is attached to it. um.bookTicker is recorded, health-monitored, normalized and read by every later consumer that needs a quote, and it is not in required_for_coverage: no contemporary first-party archive publishes a minute denominator for it over the prospective period. Nothing is substituted for that denominator, not bookDepth, not metrics, not trades, not aggTrades, not a REST snapshot and not another venue, and no wall-clock threshold takes its place in this gate. For um.funding: schedule_established(D) is true when a funding schedule source covering the whole of D has been fetched under the acquisition rules, verified against its .CHECKSUM companion and parsed, and false when that object is absent, unverified, unparseable or covers only part of D; it is a fact about the evidence and never about the venue. scheduled_settlements(D) is defined only when schedule_established(D): the settlements of D that source lists (three, at the eight-hour cadence in force at the time of writing; the count is read from the source and never assumed), and it may be empty, an established empty set meaning the source says no settlement was scheduled for D. captured_settlements(D) is the subset present in the recorder's settlements file agreeing exactly on settlement time and realised funding rate; the funding archive publishes the settlement instant, the realised rate and a funding interval, and that interval metadata is recorded where it is published. The funding archive publishes no settlement mark price. The recorder may still capture the settlement mark price from its live public source and keep its provenance, and that value is not claimed to be verified by the funding archive, is not part of funding_complete(D), is never reconstructed from mark-price candles, never matched to a nearest minute, never filled or interpolated, and never replaced by a REST value during archive reconciliation. funding_complete(D) is schedule_established(D) and every settlement in scheduled_settlements(D) being present in captured_settlements(D). There is no settlement ratio and no settlement denominator: funding_complete is a quantifier over an established set and not a quotient, so a day whose established schedule is empty is funding-complete because the universal holds over the empty set, and 0 / 0 is never evaluated; schedule_established(D), |scheduled_settlements(D)| and |captured_settlements(D)| are reported as three separate values. um.funding has no wallclock coverage: it is not divided by 1440 and the 0.990 minute-stream outage threshold does not apply to it. A day passes when both hold: (1) published_coverage(s, D) >= 0.995 for every minute-indexed required stream, and (2) funding_complete(D), the day's funding schedule established and every settlement it lists captured with exact agreement. wallclock_coverage is reported beside (1) for the minute-indexed streams; a day whose wallclock_coverage < 0.990 on any minute-indexed required stream is flagged RECORDER_OUTAGE even if it passes, and three flagged days in a window fail the gate. A missing or disagreeing scheduled settlement is not a flag and fails the day outright. Three funding cases are kept apart in the record: a source establishing that no settlement was scheduled for D makes the day funding-complete with nothing for the recorder to miss, and the zero is recorded so it is visible; a schedule that could not be established is not a zero, is never recorded as one, makes funding_complete(D) false and is reported FUNDING_SCHEDULE_UNAVAILABLE, which is not a RECORDER_OUTAGE flag and does not enter the three-flagged-days count; a scheduled settlement that is missing or disagrees fails the day outright. The funding schedule source is a monthly object, so a day inside a month whose archive has not been published yet is FUNDING_SCHEDULE_UNAVAILABLE and does not pass until that archive appears, is verified, and the reconciliation is run again for the day. That is expected evidence latency and not a recorder fault, it is not shortened by reading a REST endpoint instead, and it means the gate can become claimable later than the thirtieth day. The gate passes when 30 consecutive UTC days pass, counted from the first passing day at or after prospective_from; any day that does not pass, whether it failed or could not be judged, resets the count to zero, and the streak is recomputed from the reconciliation records every time the gate is evaluated, so a day whose schedule source appears later takes its real verdict when the reconciliation is run again for it. No price, return, funding flow, basis, profit or other economic quantity is computed by any recorder tool: settlement agreement is an equality check on published values.
reconciliation_rule: Once per UTC day, for day D-2: fetch from data.binance.vision the daily archive that publishes each minute-indexed required stream and the monthly funding archive, each with its .CHECKSUM companion, which is futures/um/daily/klines for um.kline_1m, futures/um/daily/markPriceKlines for um.markPrice, spot/daily/klines for spot.kline_1m and futures/um/monthly/fundingRate for um.funding. The recorder owns this parsing under its own semantics and imports no research checkpoint's code; it is held to the same source-integrity rules this repository already applies to historical acquisition: one allow-listed first-party host and no other, HTTPS with no credential and no signature, the .CHECKSUM companion parsed and the digest it publishes verified against the bytes received, a checksum mismatch refused rather than repaired or retried into acceptance, a cache keyed by the object's full archive path that is not read when it cannot vouch for the value it holds, a single-member archive whose one member is verified before it is extracted, an epoch unit resolved explicitly per file rather than inferred from magnitude, and only the funding layouts frozen in the recorder recognised. Then compare, minute by minute, the recorder's normalized open, high, low, close, volume and taker-buy base against the kline archive with relative tolerance 1e-9, the parity tolerance nn.multiclock already uses, and the recorder's per-minute mark open, high, low and close against the mark-price archive the same way; compare funding settlements exactly on settlement time and realised rate, and record the archive's funding interval metadata where it is published; write reconciliation/YYYY-MM-DD.json recording minutes compared, agreeing, disagreeing (listed), present only in the archive, present only in the recorder, the published-minute count that is the denominator of the coverage gate, and, because the funding condition of the coverage rule is evaluated from these records, whether the day's funding schedule was established and the settlements it lists when it was; never modify the recorder's files, because a disagreement is a finding and not a repair. The index values recorded alongside the mark observations are reconciled against futures/um/daily/indexPriceKlines and reported as a diagnostic; that comparison is not a pass condition for um.markPrice and no threshold is attached to it. um.bookTicker is recorded and normalized, and no contemporary first-party archive publishes a minute denominator for it, so it is not archive-reconciled for coverage and nothing is substituted for it.
recorder_version_policy: The recorder's source identity (nn.source_identity.source_identity: scheme, revision, dirty, source_digest), the Python and library versions, and a hostname hash are recorded on every day manifest, together with the contract id, the contract hash and the boundary state in force when the day was written. Two kinds of change are kept apart. Activation, writing prospective_from once from null to the midnight the boundary rule derives, is an edit to this file made in a separate reviewed commit, and it moves contract_hash; this schema carries no supersedes field and none is added for it, so the relation between the pre-activation and the activated identity is recorded where this repository can actually hold it, in Git history, in the amendment record of the adopted plan, and in the contract hash stamped on every day manifest. Any other change to what is acquired is a different acquisition and is a new contract file with its own contract_id, never an edit to this one. Data recorded under a hash keeps that hash on every manifest, a storage root never mixes contract hashes, and one campaign never mixes contracts.
description: Prospective, forward-only market data for the Binance USD-M BTCUSDT perpetual and Binance spot BTCUSDT, recorded from public endpoints with no credentials. Nothing under this contract has been acquired: prospective_from is unset, no minute of it is scientific evidence, and amendments A4 to A9 of the adopted implementation master plan corrected this contract's source-validity and activation semantics while that was still true.
